verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe isolated cloud sessions created and controlled programmatically, each exposing a WebSocket/CDP endpoint for Playwright or Puppeteer (docs-10, docs-19). That covers the session-management half of the story. Concurrency limits appear only in a community remark that Hyperbrowser's pricing offers twice Browserbase's concurrency, which implies published tier limits but doesn't evidence them. missing for 10: first-party documentation of per-plan concurrency limits, documented session lifecycle APIs (list/stop/status) for fleet management, evidence of running many sessions in parallel at scale.
